before: The novel chronicles Stevens, a butler at Darlington Hall who has dedicated his life to serving his master Lord Darlington. Set in the 1930s, the story begins with Stevens in his mid-50s and has been working at Darlington Hall for over 30 years. He is deeply devoted to his work and takes great pride in his profession, believing that a butler's role extends beyond mere service to provide continuity and tradition in an evolving world.  Despite his dedication, Stevens faces numerous challenges. He has few close relationships outside of work and his only companion is his father, who is also a butler at a nearby estate. As the novel progresses, Stevens's father becomes ill, forcing him to confront the reality of his own mortality and the choices he has made in life.  Simultaneously, Stevens finds himself entangled in events that challenge his beliefs about his role as a butler and his relationship with his master. Lord Darlington, a wealthy and influential man, is a Nazi sympathizer, prompting Stevens to grapple with moral implications of serving such a man. As political tensions escalate in Europe, Stevens must decide where his loyalties truly lie and what he is willing to do to uphold his sense of duty and honor.  Throughout the novel, Stevens grapples with questions of identity, loyalty and morality all against the backdrop of rapidly changing times in the 1930s. Reflecting on his life and past decisions, he confronts both personal and historical legacies. The narrative explores profound themes of human nature, duty, loyalty and identity, offering a poignant and thought-provoking examination of the human condition.
